title: Editing an existing v2 program deletes all program_workouts rows before recreating them, and recreation currently always fails (PGRST204 notes)
steps: Seed a v2 program with 3 program_workouts rows, open /program-builder?edit=<id>, walk to Confirm, tap 'Update Program' (no notes-migration workaround applied -- exercising the currently-deployed behavior).
expected: Either the update fully succeeds (all days present with the edit applied), or it fully fails leaving the ORIGINAL days untouched. Zero program_workouts rows remaining for a program that had rows before the edit must not happen.
actual: CONFIRMED data loss: program had 3 program_workouts rows before the edit; after tapping 'Update Program' (toast: failToast=true okToast=false), 0 rows remain. useUpdateProgram (useProgramQueries.js:146-170) deletes all existing ProgramWorkout rows unconditionally before looping ProgramWorkout.create for the new set; because every create call 400s on PGRST204 (notes column missing the migration that adds it), the delete lands but not a single day gets recreated -- the program is silently reduced to zero days, worse than the known create-time failure (which at least leaves nothing to lose). The UI shows 'Failed to update program' with no indication the program's days were just destroyed.

title: Assigning a library workout to a program day (drag-and-drop) always 400s — program_workouts.source_workout_id column does not exist on hosted, independent of the known notes migration
steps: In /program-builder, drag a library workout from WorkoutLibrarySidebar onto a day cell, then Create/Save (with notes stripped to bypass the known migration gap).
expected: Either the assign succeeds and source_workout_id is stored, or the app never writes a column that does not exist.
actual: A direct insert/update of program_workouts with source_workout_id set fails: PGRST204 "Could not find the 'source_workout_id' column of 'program_workouts' in the schema cache". Checked supabase/migrations/*.sql: no migration ever adds source_workout_id (unlike locked/override_source, added by 20260902000000_program_workout_override.sql). ProgramBuilder.jsx:404,411 sets it on every drag-drop assign; WorkoutDetail.jsx:800-802 reads it defensively (falls back silently, no crash there). So every drag-and-drop assign-then-save in the wizard 400s today, for a second, independent reason beyond the known notes PGRST204 — fixing the notes migration alone will NOT fix Assign-then-save.
repro: ui-audit/overnight/areas/train-programs/scripts/r1-11.mjs (surfaced as an uncaught PGRST204 on the first run before the field was removed from the seed helper)
evidence: Direct testDb() insert into program_workouts with source_workout_id set threw: {code: 'PGRST204', message: "Could not find the 'source_workout_id' column of 'program_workouts' in the schema cache"}. grep -rn source_workout_id supabase/migrations/ -> no results.
why: Not reachable from the app. The column really is missing on hosted (no migration adds source_workout_id), but ProgramBuilder never sends it. handleSubmit (ProgramBuilder.jsx:425-436) rebuilds each workout with an explicit field whitelist (day_index, title, focus, notes, exercises, cardio_sessions, week_number), so the source_workout_id set in drag-drop state (:404,:411) is dropped before useCreateProgram/useUpdateProgram insert. Those are the only program_workouts creators (grep: useProgramQueries.js:127,156). The attacker's PGRST204 came from its own seed helper inserting source_workout_id directly, not from the app. So a library-workout drag onto a day, then save, fails only on the known notes PGRST204. It is a duplicate of the known migration 20260928000000 issue and will work once that is applied. Side note, not a bug: WorkoutDetail.jsx:800-802's source_workout_id branch is dead code (always undefined) and falls back safely.

title: Offline mid-Enroll: no error toast ever appears, and the outcome after reconnecting is inconsistent — sometimes the enroll silently never happens
steps: Open Enroll dialog, fill a starting weight, context.setOffline(true), tap Start Program (the confirm button inside the dialog), wait, then context.setOffline(false) and wait.
expected: A clear failure toast ('Failed to enroll') while offline, dialog stays open with weights preserved, and a manual retry succeeds exactly once.
actual: Run across 3 attempts (one intentional re-run per the flaky-result rule, plus one diagnostic re-run): errToast never appeared in any run (no "Failed to enroll" text). Behavior after reconnecting was NOT consistent: one run resolved correctly (enroll succeeded exactly once, dialog closed) after ~6-8s once back online; two runs left the enrollment never created at all (0 rows) with no error shown, dialog state ambiguous. Weights typed into the form were preserved on-screen (135 retained) across runs, so nothing visibly vanishes, but the athlete gets zero signal of failure either way — the UI looks identical whether the enroll is about to silently succeed, silently never complete, or (rarely) resolve. No console/network problems were ever recorded in any run (React Query mutation swallows the offline state cleanly, never surfacing an onError).
evidence: Three script runs, differing outcomes: run1 disabled=true throughout offline then resolved on reconnect (enrolled); run2 disabled=false throughout, enrollmentsFinal=0 after reconnect; run3 (diagnostic) disabled=false throughout, a GET to program_enrollments returned 200 mid-offline (likely served from HTTP cache, not a real round-trip), enrollmentsFinal=0.
suspectFile: src/pages/ProgramDetail.jsx:168-183 (handleEnroll/useEnrollInProgram) — no client-side timeout, no offline-detection guard, and useEnrollInProgram (useProgramQueries.js:183-240) does a preliminary read (ProgramEnrollment.filter) before the write, whose own offline/retry behavior is unclear and appears inconsistent across runs.
why: The half that says the outcome is inconsistent (enroll sometimes silently never happens) is a harness artifact. The attacker's script opened the dialog via nth(1) and clicked the '.last()' Start Program button while the iphone-sim keyboard was up, so the first tap only dismissed the keyboard. An ONLINE control run without a blur also created 0 enrollments. With the input blurred before the tap, 2 of 2 offline runs behaved identically: the button read 'Starting...' and stayed disabled for the full 10s offline, with no toast and no hint about the connection. After reconnect the paused mutation resumed, exactly 1 enrollment was created, and the dialog closed. So no data loss and no double-enroll, but the confirmed part is the same stuck-spinner gap fixed in fuel (f2590dcd). React Query's default networkMode pauses useEnrollInProgram rather than failing it, so onError ('Failed to enroll', ProgramDetail.jsx:180) never fires.
fixHint: src/pages/ProgramDetail.jsx:797-799: when enrollMutation.isPaused, show 'Offline - starts when you're back online' instead of 'Starting...' (same pattern as fuel f2590dcd).

title: WeekTemplateSwap's `touched` (already-logged) set is a client-cached React Query snapshot with no invalidation hook for writes made elsewhere -- applying a template right after a concurrent log can overwrite an already-logged day
steps: Open /weekly-schedule (WeekTemplateSwap's `touched` query fires and caches with the target date NOT logged yet), then (simulating a concurrent write via testDb, e.g. a log finished on another device/tab) insert a workout_logs row for a day later this week (Wednesday, chosen to avoid a same-day confound from other agents sharing this test account and logging against 'today'), then immediately -- no reload -- open the template picker and apply a folder for the week.
expected: The logged date stays untouched by the template because it's logged (`touched` should include it) -- the apply mutation should re-derive touched server-side, or at minimum re-fetch before computing the plan, rather than trusting a client snapshot that predates the log write.
actual: CONFIRMED: the targetDate (2026-09-30) program_workouts row was rewritten with override_source='template:OVN-train-programs-r1-09 folder' despite a workout_logs row for that date existing in the DB before Apply was tapped. useApplyWeekTemplate/planTemplateWeek (useWeekTemplate.js:36-45,68-84) compute the plan purely from the client's cached `touched` Set (WeekTemplateSwap.jsx:29-47, React Query keyed [weekTemplateRows,user,programId,first]); a workout_logs write made through any channel other than this component's own query invalidation (a testDb insert, a second tab, a different device) never triggers a refetch, so the plan can silently include and overwrite an already-logged day. No pageerror (problems=0).

suspectFile: src/components/program/WeekTemplateSwap.jsx:29-47 (touched query, no dependency on a just-logged signal), src/hooks/useWeekTemplate.js:36-45 (templateDates/planTemplateWeek trust the caller-supplied touched Set), :68-84 (useApplyWeekTemplate mutationFn does no server-side re-check before writing)
why: The mechanism is real, but the trigger is harness-only and the impact is not data loss. The attacker inserted a workout_logs row for a date 2 days in the future via testDb while /weekly-schedule sat open, with no navigation, focus or visibility change. In the app the QueryClient uses defaults (App.jsx:58: staleTime 0, refetchOnMount, refetchOnWindowFocus), so logging on the same device (/workout-detail unmounts the schedule) or returning to the PWA from another app/device refetches weekTemplateRows and touched before the picker opens. The only remaining window is another device finishing a log while this phone stays foregrounded on Schedule, and that log would have to be for a future day. Even then, useApplyWeekTemplate only rewrites the program_workouts plan row (title/exercises/locked), and the workout_logs row, the ground truth, is untouched. I didn't re-run it, because the script pauses the real active baseline enrollment. Low-cost hardening if wanted: re-query touched inside useApplyWeekTemplate's mutationFn.

title: Rapid Pause/Resume taps: buttons have no isPending guard, but final status matched last intent in this run
steps: On /program/:id with an active enrollment, fire 3 near-simultaneous Pause clicks (no await between), then once the UI shows Resume, fire 2 near-simultaneous Resume clicks.
expected: Final status is deterministic and matches the last action (Pause buttons have no disabled={statusMutation.isPending} guard per ProgramDetail.jsx:448-461, same shape as fuel WeeklyPlanCard double-approve).
actual: afterPauseX3 status=paused, afterResumeX2 status=active. finalDeterministic=true. No pageerror. Confirmed by code read: neither Pause nor Resume button passes disabled={statusMutation.isPending} (ProgramDetail.jsx:428,454), so a genuinely concurrent double-tap (both requests in flight before either resolves) is possible and would be last-network-response-wins, not last-click-wins -- this run's clicks mostly serialized fast enough that the result matched intent, but the missing guard is real and independently confirmed by code, matching the same unguarded-mutation shape flagged elsewhere in this area (r1-02) and in fuel (WeeklyPlanCard).
suspectFile: src/pages/ProgramDetail.jsx:428 (Resume button), :454 (Pause button) — no isPending disable; useUpdateEnrollmentStatus (useProgramQueries.js:383-396) has no optimistic-concurrency check.
why: There's no bug. The missing isPending guard on Pause/Resume (ProgramDetail.jsx:428,454) is real, but useUpdateEnrollmentStatus (useProgramQueries.js:383-395) writes an absolute status value, so repeated taps are idempotent. Pause lives behind the Manage disclosure, and Resume only renders after the paused refetch, so a 'pause then resume in flight at once' needs two deliberate taps across a re-render. The attacker's own run ended in the intended state (paused, then active). The worst case is a duplicate 'Program paused' toast.
